newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia wants to reopen oil deal with Swiss NPL.
newsitem.headline: Georgia wants to reopen oil deal with Swiss NPL.

text.p: Georgia wants to renegotiate an oil contract with Swiss company National Petroleum Limited because of low production levels in a project the firm is involved in, the presidential press office said on Wednesday.
A statement said President Eduard Shevardnadze had met National Petroleum President Bruce Rappaport on Tuesday evening.

The statement said Shevardnadze expressed his displeasure with oil output levels from a joint venture set up between Geneva-based National Petroleum and the Georgian government oil company Gruzneft two years ago.

The joint venture, Ioris Veli, has been producing 500 tonnes of crude oil per day (3,665 bpd) from the Samgori field in the east of the Caucasus country, Gruzneft Chairman Revaz Tevzadze told Reuters.
"We are not satisfied with the speed of production," Tevzadze said. "We would like to see an increase up to between 800 and 1,000 tonnes per day."
He said that under the existing contact, Gruzneft had too little influence in day-to-day operations of the venture. He said National Petroleum had invested $22 million in the project.
"They invested quite a bit of money in the project and they are taking all the important decisions," he said.
The statement from Shevardnadze's press office said the two sides had set up a working committee to try and seek ways of boosting production.
He said total reserves at Samgori were estimated at from seven to 15 million tonnes. National Petroleum officials were not available for comment.
